utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Thanks for filling it out. We give this form to everyone once a year regardless of why they come in. It helps us provide better care. Is it okay if I take a look at what you put down?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, let's see. It looks that you put-- You drink alcohol at least four times a week on average-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and you usually have three to four drinks when you do drink.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Usually three drinks and glasses of wine.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. That's at least 12 drinks a week.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Just so you know, my role, um, when we talk about alcohol use, is just to share information about risk and to help patients who want help. This is different than telling them what I think they should do. I don't do that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh, what else can you tell me about your drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I usually drink when I'm at home trying to unwind and I drink while I'm watching a movie. And sometimes, um, I take a bath but I also drink when I take a bath sometimes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, can I share with you some information on alcohol use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, there has been a lot of research on alcohol use and the guidelines we use in this country says that having seven or more drinks per week can raise the risk of health problems for women.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm. Seven?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Wow. I knew my doctor didn't like me drinking the amount that I did but I didn't know that seven was the limit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, you're surprised to hear that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes. What-what kind of health problems?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well things like heart disease, cancer, liver problems, uh, stomach pains, insomnia. Unfortunately, uh, people who drink at a risky level are more likely to be diagnosed with depression and alcohol can make depression worse or harder to treat.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm. Well, that's not good news.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, how do you think your drinking relates to the depression you've experienced?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, I drink sometimes when I'm feeling down and I find it more interesting and not so blur.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And how do you feel after you drink?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, then I feel blur again.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, there are some answers on this form here. Uh, less than monthly you drank more than you intended to.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes on occasion.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And sometimes you feel guilty after you drink.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sometimes I just don't like how much I drink. I sometimes finish a bottle in one night.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you're not proud of finishing a bottle?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, it's not like I get crazy or anything but I just don't like the amount that I'm drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. By the way, binge drinking is defined for women as having more than, uh, three drinks and there are about five drinks in a bottle. So, you enjoy drinking wine because it helps make things, uh, a little bit more interesting when you're feeling down but at the same time you don't like drinking when you have more than you want it to and then the depression returns after you drink.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yes, sometimes I feel worse after drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Where do you wanna go from here? What do you wanna change about your drinking habits?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that I'm ready to cut down to seven drinks a week. That seems like a lot but I would consider cutting back to two drinks a night. I think that would be my goal.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: If I gave you a scale from 0 to 10, 0 being not ready at all to cut back on drinking and 10 being very ready, what number would you be at?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd say an eight.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Why do you think it's not something less like a six?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I'm more ready than a six because I'm ready to cut back on my drinking and I don't wanna make my depression any worse.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What would help you cut back to two drinks?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe having less wine in the house.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Having less wine in the house will help?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What else besides drinking helps you relax and unwind in the evenings?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I like to watch movies, read a book, and take a bath but sometimes I drink when I take a bath.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, it's not just wine that helps you relax. Um, there's reading a book, watching a movie, and taking a hot bath too.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it sounds like you have some reasons to cut back on drinking and you have ways to relax besides drinking and it sounds like you're pretty ready to cut back.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. I'd be interested to see how well you do on your goal in the next few weeks. Would you be willing to come back and talk to me about it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. So, let's see how well you're doing with these new meds.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And before you leave, uh, is it okay if we go over this screening form that you filled out today on your alcohol use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Uh, thanks for filling this out. Uh, looks like you use alcohol two to three days a week?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, but only on the weekend.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And then when you do drink alcohol, you typically have five or six drinks.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Uh, maybe a couple more.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the reason why I like to talk to patients when they fill out this form is because sometimes, uh, alcohol use can impact our health. Um, and my role is to be helpful. I can share some information with you about alcohol use, um, but I don't tell anyone what to do. It's always up to the patient to decide what they wanna do about their drinking. Um, so is it okay if we talk a little bit more about your alcohol use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, uh, are you saying I drink too much?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How would you define drinking too much?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I-- If-if I was getting fallen down drunk or if I drink every night. Um, it's not like I get sloppy drunk or anything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Well, in this country, the guidelines are men can drink up to 14 drinks a week or up to four on one occasion and still be low risk.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So I'm already at the week limit. And then I have four beers a night. Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So a limit of four a night doesn't feel right to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I have five or six beers when I go out with friends to a bar. It's not a problem for me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're not alone in feeling that way. Uh, binge drinking can feel normal to some people.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I don't consider my drinking binge drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't chug a lot of beers in a row. I have about five or six beers throughout the entire evening.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Well, technically, we define binge drinking as having more than four drinks on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But I'm healthy. What health problems are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, uh, we know if someone binge drinks over time, there's kind of two categories of risk. There's the short-term risk where someone who binge drinks is more likely to fall down, hurt themselves through an accident, uh, they're more likely to drive while under the influence. Uh, but over the long term, binge drinking can also, uh, cause things like heart disease, uh, different kinds of cancer, liver problems obviously, and then even mental health issues like depression and anxiety are more likely to happen.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know about those things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Can I ask you, uh, what do you like about drinking alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I-I like beer. I like the way it tastes, I like the way it makes me feel. Uh, like when I'm around friends and it's not a problem for me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And so what about your drinking do you not like or is there anything that worries you about your drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, that was fine until I came here, uh, but now that I know about the health risk, uh, I have something I gotta think about.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, on one hand, you like how beer tastes, uh, it's part of your social life to some extent, um, but on the other hand, you don't like the idea of it posing risks to your health over the long term?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: E-exactly.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So weighing those things, you know, what you like about your drinking, what you don't like about your drinking, uh, where do you wanna go from here? Uh, what would you like to change about your drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm, I'm not sure. Uh, something I have to think about.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, how about hypothetically if I were to ask you, how would your drinking have to impact your life in order for you to be ready to change your drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, I don't know. Maybe if I got sick or something, uh, maybe I'd wanna change things then.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So if you experienced a negative consequence from your drinking, uh, that would feel meaningful to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I like to give this handout to patients. Uh, it defines risky drinking, it talks about what the consequences are, uh, and it also lists signs of what an alcohol use disorder is. So thanks again for taking the time to fill this out and being honest with me, uh, to talk about it. I provide better care, uh, when I know about my patient's substance use. When we come back for a three-month follow-up appointment for your ADHD, I'd also like to talk to you and check in about your alcohol use too, if that's okay with you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sounds good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, great. See you next time.

utterances.text: Oh, it's a nice place. It's close to work. It's good living with a mate.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So, in terms of being supportive and a sort of support you're gonna need to make these changes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What's your thinking around that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That's the thing, isn't it? I am-- I don't know if it's the best place for me to be if I'm gonna make those changes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And Tristan is a good flatmate.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I have no-- We're going in different-different directions now. He doesn't have the same kind of responsibilities I have and stuff, and so-- And I can't expect him to change his whole life around, just because I wanna change mine.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just-- I don't know how keen I am to move in with my- with my aunty and uncle, though.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. You're good to explore, but I just want to ask you about, how much does Chris-Christian-Christian know-- Tristan know about you changing your life? What does he really know about the changes you wanna make?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I sit down and talk with him, asked him for, um, for support and stuff and he's fully, he says fully he'll be there for me. But, like I said, he's, um, he's in a different place in his life than I am in mine.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: He doesn't have kids.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: He doesn't-- I don't know if he can really understand what it means to me. Um, he's a good mate.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What are some of the pros and cons about moving in with whāna, moving in with your auntie and uncle?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: The food would be good. Um, I get- I get support with-- my whānau is really supportive, but I'm- I'm worried about losing- I'm worried about losing my freedom. I'm worried about, um, about them taking over, or, you know what I mean? I have a freedom where I am now, I'm in charge of myself. That would probably be really good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: In terms of that freedom and in charge of yourself, and the changes that we're talking about, and building your own family, and to enable you to do that, where do some of that freedom stuff sit with re-engaging back with your whānau and your children, your partner? Is it something you're gonna wanna hang on to, or how you're going to manage that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't wanna hang on to freedom if it this- if it means that I lose my kids. Um, I'm just, uh, I'm just worried about-- I'm worried about if I move in with family, that they, even if their intentions are good-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. I'll do anything to get my kids back.

video_title: The Effective School Counselor With a Lower-Risk Teen: Motivational Interviewing Demonstration

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, Laura.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Thanks for coming in. Um, so, I'm not sure how much you know already about sort of what you're doing here. If it's okay, I'll give you a little rundown.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, basically, we're here, I'm just gonna talk to you for a little bit about sort of what your goals are for your life, um, get to know you a little bit better and talk about some different behaviors that you might be engaging in. It's not my job at all to judge you or to try and change you, you know. Basically, I'm gonna talk to you about how things are going, any changes you might want to make in your life, how I could help you with that, and just what I can do that's going to be most beneficial for you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Does that sound okay?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right, so, I guess just to get started, can you tell me a little bit about yourself?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, my name is Laura. I'm 17 years old, and I'm a senior in high school.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And, what kinds of things do you plan for your life?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, hopefully, go to college, get, you know, good enough grades to go to college.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's great.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Do you have a plan as to where you might want to go or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I'm not sure yet. Maybe a few schools in the area, I'm looking maybe to apply out-of-state.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, maybe move away for college.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Cool.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, kind of keeping your options open.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. And, do you have an idea about what you might want to study or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, maybe um, pre-law.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, wow. Okay, that's exciting.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right, cool. Uh, what do you like to do for fun?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, um, on the weekends I like to hang out with my friends, maybe go to like a party, or go to the mall to shop, or if there's like a school-related event, we'll go to like a football game or-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -something like that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You like to have a good time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And, you have a lot of friends or a few close people, or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I would say like a moderate amount. I'm not really-really popular or like, I have no friends.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I'm like normal.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's a good way to be, right?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right, so, um, it sounds like, in general, your-- Things are going pretty well for you. How are your grades right now?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, they're pretty good, As and Bs. So, I'm doing okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Through college.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. Well, one thing I want to ask about is, you know, different people have sort of different values or things that are important to them. They might, you know, be really close with family or really have, you know, their friends as being something particularly important. So, I'm gonna show you just a few things on this sheet, and if you can look at them all. So, there's things like belonging, community, cultural identity, family, friendship, modesty, religion, respect, self-determination and spirituality. Which of those do you think is sort of important to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, family definitely, uh, friendship, and belonging.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What's important to you about your family?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I-I love them, so I want them to think well of me-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and I want them to, um, be accepting and love me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have brothers or sisters?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I have one sister.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, great. And, how about friendship?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Friendship, um, I've-I've grown close to many people that I care about. So, I would like them to be accepting of me as well.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. So, being a good friend and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -having people who are good friends, too, is important. And then, what about belonging? You mentioned that one too.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, just a sense of like fitting in and not-- And like getting accepted-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -in general, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Wanting to be part of a group-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and kinda. Okay, great. All right, well, one of the things I wanna talk about is, you know, um, you mentioned that you'd like to go out with friends and-and party, and that sort of a thing. And, I'm curious, when you're out in the parties, do you ever have any alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, not much, maybe like one or two drinks at the most.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell me a little bit about how alcohol fits into your overall social scene?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I pretty much just have a drink to just have it like, so it looks like I'm drinking, even though I'm not.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So maybe people won't bug me about drinking or something.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, you're kinda getting pressure from other people who are drinking, and it feels easier for you to-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah just-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -kinda hold a drink.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -have one there and pretending to have it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And, do you think that, um, this is most weekends or occasionally? How-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -often do you think that you are around alcohol.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe one or two weekends a month at the most?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not really much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, one or two weekends a month you're in a situation where there is alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And what sort of situations are you in?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, just I guess, at a party or something, someone's house.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Or, even if it's not a party, like a small social gathering, maybe there'll be like a few beers around-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -or something.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, mainly, just kinda hanging out with friends.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Pretty much, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Are you ever, um, places where there are parents around or-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -or mostly just-just with the kids?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mostly just with us, but, sometimes I'll go to like a close friend's house and like I'm close to a family as well. So, we'll all just hang out.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And, what about driving?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, like drunk driving?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Do you ever go anywhere in a car after you've had any alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, definitely not. I've never drunk-driven, and I've never been in a car with a drunk driver.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, that's something that you've sort of made a decision about. It sound like you—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, because I know that's extremely dangerous, so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What do you know about how that's dangerous?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, alcohol definitely impairs your judgment. So, I mean, driving under the influence of alcohol can lead to like crashes and accidents and things like that, so I'd rather not be in that situation.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you're really are trying to be safe and-and make sure that-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -you're not putting yourself-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -in those situations? That's great. You know, it's-it's tough to do sometimes, and I really commend you for being able to-to stick with that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, you mentioned, you pretty much will like hold a drink or maybe have a drink or two. What do you thinks is the most alcohol you've ever had in-in one day?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not more than two drinks.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, the-the absolute most-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -was two? Okay. And, what kinds of things do you like about alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I've never really been drunk-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -so, I can't really say that I like that feeling or not, but, it's just like-- I mean, you're just in a good mood.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, it just kind of makes you feel relaxed or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, relaxed.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Uh, anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, no, not really. Like I said, I don't drink that much-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I-I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And, any not-so-good things about alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, definitely, yeah. I mean, when I'm at parties and stuff and it's getting a little later, some people, um, that drink-- Like, drank too much, they start throwing up, or they get hurt, or they're really loud and obnoxious, and that's not fun for anybody.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So, you've seen a lot of other kids who-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -had some consequences-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and decided that's not for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Got it. I-I can understand that. [chuckles] Uh, any other things that you can think of?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, no, I mean, I've never, you know, been friends with anybody that's gotten into like a serious accident and stuff. It's just-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -very, like, obnoxious things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, so, you know, as someone who's not 21 yet, it is-- Underage drinking is something that's not legal-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and it is something that is considered pretty risky. So, I wonder what you think about that, just in terms of how it fits into your life.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I know it's definitely risky, but, I mean, I guess, we still do it. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh. So, it's kind of something that you're—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's just there.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It's just there? Okay. And, I'm curious, you mentioned, you know, your friends are important to you, and your family's important to you, and, sort of fitting in is important to you. How does alcohol play a role with that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, definitely not in my family life, because my parents don't really condone-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -alcohol use, but, friendships, I mean, when I'm hanging out with my friends, or we're at a party or something, there's usually alcohol involved.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, from your family perspective, the drinking is not something that fits very well?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And with friends, you feel like it's easier to-to hang out with alcohol, or maybe you wouldn't have as much fun, or your friends wouldn't like you as much or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess, I mean, since it's just there.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -it ties in with the whole belonging thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, when you think about your drinking and, sort of, looking forward in 5 years or 10 years, how do you think that drinking might fit in with your life?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, it probably will have a very small role, if any-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -in my life, considering I have big plans for my future. So.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Can you expand on that a little bit more? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I mean, I don't think I would be, you know, drinking as much or going to parties as much if I'm studying for school, or in college, or trying to get in law school and things like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so, the-the alcohol is something that might make it harder to reach your goals?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, so, when you're sort of looking ahead, how often do you think you might be drinking, say, when you get to college?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, maybe less than I am now. I mean, I don't drink much anyway, so-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -maybe, like, one drink every once in a blue moon.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, you sort of have a plan to cut back on-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -your drinking eventually?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: For sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: How might that go?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I guess right now I would try to stop in high school, and once I get older, maybe just like, socially once in a while, but not anything big or anything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, so, you don't feel the need to make any major changes, but you feel like you could make some adjustments that would make it easier or—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Definitely, yeah. That's a good word.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. How important is it to you to make some adjustments to your drinking, on a scale of 1 to 10? Where 1 is not at all important, not something you're thinking about, and 10 is most important thing.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe a five or six.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And why did you say five or six rather than like two or three?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because, um, it's not something I do not care about at all, but it's not something that's just constantly on my mind that I want to change about myself.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it is something you have thought about or something.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And, how confident are you that you could make a change if you decide you wanted to on that same scale?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I'm pretty confident that I can considering that I'm not really an alcohol user per se.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'm not really into that whole scene, so, it's-it's not gonna bedifficult for me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, what number do you think you'd say?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, on a scale of 1 to 10-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -if I can quit or not?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe like an 8 or 9.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, and why'd you say 8 or 9 rather than even like 5 or 6?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Because, like I said, it's not a big part of my life. So, it's not really that difficult

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, kind of keeping that in mind, it sounds like, um, you do have sort of a-a vague plan to make some adjustments in your drinking at some point-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and, it's moderately important to you. It's something you would like to do because you have these big goals for yourself, and you actually feel very confident that you could be successful with it. What sort of goal do you think might be good to set for today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, probably to stop, maybe next party I go to, not have a drink at all.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, do you feel pretty confident that you could just stop completely?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I can just tell my friends-- My pa-- My friends aren't really that pressuring.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's just like outside people that I don't really know that well.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I could just tell them, "Hey, I don't feel like having a drink today."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What-what might be some benefits of following through with that goal?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, definitely, I'll have like all my senses there and I'll be aware of everything that's going on.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, health concerns, I guess. I know alcohol is bad for your health.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, that would be one.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it's-- It sounds like you're actually pretty comfortable with setting a goal of not drinking anymore a-at least at the next part? and seeing how it goes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Do you think it would be all right if we met again to kinda check in on how it goes and-and see if it's working out for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right, great. And then, i-it sounds like some of the benefits you're expecting are, um, health benefits-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -having an easier time with achieving your academic and career goals, and just sort of not having to deal with some of the consequences that your peers do.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, very good. Um, is there anything else that you think would be important for me to know?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, how would you, um, advise me to like get maybe my friends to stop drinking?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, that's a great question. So, a lot of times, kids who are trying to cut back, it's harder if their friends are still drinking, and one of the easiest things is trying to have more activities that don't involve alcohol, but-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -of course, that's harder if you're not the one planning. So, some of the things that can be useful if you're at a party say, um, and there's already alcohol there, and there are other kids that maybe aren't your closest friends, um, some of the things that I would recommend since you're interested are, you know, carrying around a different drink that looks like it has alcohol in it. So, you know, even carrying an empty beer bottle or beer can or, you know, if people are having a mixed drink, just having the coke, say-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it's perhaps taking you away from things that are more important to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it doesn't feel good?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And so, it sounds like there's a bit of a dilemma there, because-- And I guess we should be clear, it's not the occasional drink that's an issue. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you've perhaps never seen it in that light before.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. And, i-it's just, it's really hard to take in right now. I mean, yeah. I-I've never thought about it like this. And, so, you know, I-I do feel kind of worried.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I-it seems like it-it would be quite a hard pattern to change.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, i-it's part of my routine right now, and, you know, I-I don't want to sacrifice something I enjoy, but, you know, I'm trying really hard, you know, to be a good mom. I'm-I'm trying to, you know, go-go back to school. I'm trying to work. So, I don't know how I can do all of that if I don't have a way to enjoy myself or relax, you know?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, it seems like it would be really difficult to change because it's something that's really important to you right now.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: But on the other hand, it does sound like there are things that you- that you value that you don't want the drinking to interfere with.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, I guess I'm wondering if you've given any thought to other ways in which you could cope with stress without relying on the drinking so much.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know, if there was some way that I could relieve some of my stress, I think I would feel better, and, you know, maybe at night, I wouldn't feel like I had to unwind in the same way.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, if you could somehow tackle some of these stressful issues, um, that could make a difference, and, what-what would that be, for example?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, you know, probably my biggest problem is just childcare. You know, my mom normally watches my son, but she's been kind of backing out lately. And so, I'm worrying, am I going to have to call into work today, am-am I going to have to miss class? You know, so, you know, worrying about that really stresses me out, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, having more reliable childcare could make a big difference.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it sounds like your mom has been an option in the past, but perhaps not so much anymore.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, she watches him so much. I think she's just probably getting stressed out too. And, I feel bad because, you know, it's not her son, so i-it shouldn't be her problem, but, I need something that I can rely on better.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, one thing that could make a big difference is if you could figure out some sort of more reliable, affordable childcare, and that would help you not want to drink as much.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, most of my problems always go back to money. You know, i-if I had more money, I could afford daycare, I could work less hours, you know? So, yeah. It's-it's normally related to money.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. It-it sounds like, um, you know, money could make a big difference, and you are working full time and trying to go to school to address that in the long run. Um, but on the other hand, you know, it sounds like you have some other ideas of cope- of how you might cope with stress better. Um, so, I guess I'm-I'm wondering, given our conversation so far, kind of where you are with everything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, we started off talking about how your drinking has sort of drifted into a risky area, and it would be advisable to cut back. Um, but it sounds like you feel like that's fairly important to you and not something you necessarily want to do. But on the other hand, we've talked about ways in which that perhaps could be made a bit easier, but I'm not sure if you're ready to tackle that or pursue that right now. I'm just kind of wondering where you are.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I'm ready to consider changing my drinking, but, as far as actually doing it, I-I don't know. I mean, I have a lot of problems that I'm trying to work out right now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, um, it would perhaps be helpful if you could narrow it down to just one thing, and what would that be?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Childcare, probably.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah. It sounds like from everything you're saying, that keeps coming up as one of the main issues. Um, so there may be some resources I can point you towards, but I'm- guess I'm wondering, have you looked into alternatives, more affordable, reliable childcare?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not really. I mean, I just normally see if my mom can watch my son, so, you know, I haven't really looked around.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, one thing you could consider is talking to one of our social workers, they sort of specialize in helping people who have a lot on their plate identifying resources that they may need, uh, things you haven't thought of or aren't aware of. So, I don't know, would you be interested in doing something like that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Great. Well, I can definitely set you up with that, and you can-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -um, try to tackle, um, your childcare issue, um, with some assistance. Is there anything else you'd like to do, um, for example, would you be interested in talking with me again, um, just as things progress?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I-I think I would. I mean, it's-it's been nice to just talk about everything that's going on.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So, these are not problems that are going to go away in a week. It's going to take some time to resolve. Okay, great. So, um, it sounds like we have a couple of things, uh, to pursue.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Anything-anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-mm

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Would you be interested in perhaps thinking about setting a goal with respect to your drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I could at least try to going back to one drink a night instead of two.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Try to cut back a bit and see how that goes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I-I don't know how it's going to go, especially with trying to cut back on smoking already, but, I mean, I can try.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, you can give it a go and, I think doing managing, you might just learn a little bit about how easy or difficult it's going to be, and-and also what it's like to cope with stress in other ways.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it sounds like we have two avenues to pursue, anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that sounds good. So, why don't we meet again in a couple of weeks and you kind of update me on how cutting back on your drinking has gone, and also, what it was like when you met with a social worker? Sound good?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, great. I look forward to talking next time.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

video_title: Adolescent brief intervention: "Jacob"

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, Jacob, everything looks very normal on your physical exam. Do you have any questions for me?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I see that you filled out our, um, alcohol and drug questionnaire. Is it okay if we go through this together?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What we talk about is confidential. I only tell your parents about what we say if you give your permission or if I become worried about a danger to-to you or to someone else. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, let's take a look. So I see that you have marked that you sometimes use alcohol, and that you have used alcohol to relax, feel better about yourself or fit in. Do you mind telling me a little bit more about your alcohol use?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's not a big deal. Sometimes with my friends, we'll drink a few beers and when we're hanging out or when we're at a party, and sometimes rum and cokes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so how many do you usually have at a time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, three or four, probably. I don't keep track.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And how often?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, probably about once or twice a month.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, you drink with friends, sort of three or four beers or mixed drinks, one or two times a month. How long have you been doing that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Probably since last October.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, for about six months. I'm curious. What do you like about drinking alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: What do I like about it?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don't know. It's just fun to drink with my friends, like when we're at a party at someone else's house, and we're drinking with other people that we don't know. It tastes good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, it sounds like you feel relaxed and have fun when you're drinking with friends and you like the taste.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I'm also curious, are there any parts about your alcohol use that you don't like?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don't like when I get sick in the mornings 'cause of hangovers and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -when I start throwing up, that's not- I don't like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Have you ever experienced a-a blackout, like when you've been drinking and you wake up and you don't remember what happened?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, but that happened to someone I know, though.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And have you had any problems related to-to your drinking alcohol, like at home or school or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, one time I missed first period of school 'cause I had a hangover and I was late getting up.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm, mom got mad at me 'cause I wouldn't get out of bed and she said she knew I had a hangover.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Have you told your mother that you drink with your friends?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, but I got grounded for two weeks after that. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So more negative things about your drinking, like getting into trouble with your mom and missing a class at school when you had a hangover?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, but I only missed school once.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I see on the questionnaire that you have not ridden in a car with someone who's been drinking and you haven't driven a car, um, after you've been drinking. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's great. And I hope you continue to avoid those things. As your doctor, I want you to know that I'm concerned about your drinking. When teens drink, things can go wrong, like injuring yourself. Even when you don't drink too excess, though, your brain is still developing and is very sensitive to the effects of alcohol.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's why I recommend that all my adolescent patients not drink at all. So if you were thinking today about how ready you feel to stop drinking alcohol on a scale of zero to ten, with zero not being ready at all and ten feeling very ready, what number would you pick?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, probably a five.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: A five? So, I'm curious. Why didn't you pick a lower number like a two or three that would mean you're only a little bit ready to stop drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I guess I'm just tired of getting in trouble.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What could you do to avoid getting into trouble?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, not drink.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: [chuckles] Have you ever tried not drinking or stopping drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What some people your age do is try stopping drinking for a period of time just to see what that feels like.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I could probably do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, how long do you think you could go without drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Do you think you could go two months without drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, probably.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What things would make it easier for you to not drink?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I could probably drink something else when my friends are drinking, like just coke.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Anything else to make things easier for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I can probably hang out with some of my friends who don't drink or inviting them to parties and having fun 'cause not everyone drinks at parties.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anybody in your life that you can talk to about this, who give you some support for not drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. The-- My friends who don't drink would probably be happy that I'm not drinking either and yes, they'd support me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great. So you've come up with some reasons to stop drinking, like having hangovers and throwing up and getting into trouble. And you've developed some strategies to-to try to not drink, like spending more time with friends who don't drink or having non-alcoholic drinks when people around you are drinking alcohol. I think that's a great plan. I'm really proud of you for giving this a try. How about if I have you make an appointment for two months from now and then I'll see you back and we can see how things are going?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, Nick. Thank you for completing the CRAFFT questionnaire. I also appreciate you sharing some information about yourself.

utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.text: sI see from the questionnaire, did you have got in trouble while using alcohol? Can you tell me more about that?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, Andrea, thanks for coming in.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hi. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So I don't know how much you know already about sort of my role here and why you're even here. So I thought I'd start by telling you a little bit about myself.

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: Basically, my job is to meet with all of the students. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Does that sound okay?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.text: All right. So why don't we start by you telling me a little bit about yourself?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, neat.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm also in the-- I'm a bit of a band geek. [laughter] I play, you know, in the wind ensemble and the jazz band, things like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Wow. You really are involved in music.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, [crosstalk].

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I started playing about 10 years ago, actually.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Wow.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I started on the violin first, and then I went on, explored a little with the piano, clarinet, finally found the tenor sax, and yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Very cool. I've always wanted to be good at music. [laughter] All right. So it sounds like you're in band and a-a few other musical ensembles, any other hobbies you have or things you like to do for fun?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, you know, just hanging out with my friends or go to the beach, things like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Just kind of everyday sort of stuff?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah [laughs].

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me a little bit about your family.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, well I have one older brother he's about eight and a half old- years older than me. My parents, and I have a dog [laughs].

utterances.text: Cute. What kind of dog?

utterances.text: Oh, nice. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: My big boy.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: [laughs] Very fun. All right. And how are things going in school for you?

utterances.text: Okay, great, so you're doing well. What sorts of goals do you have for after college- oh, after high school?

utterances.text: Oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But I mean, that might not happen. And then I'd like to go on and become a doctor. Study psychology and then become a psychiatrist or something.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, you have some pretty big dreams.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's great. That's really exciting to think about that-

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: Yeah. Well, I think community and belonging, I kind of related them. Um, you know how I said I was in the marching band?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I really, you know, I really enjoy being in that team setting of, you know, being with other people and all working toward- together towards that one goal.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.text: And sort of a-a sense of purpose in a way.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes, purpose.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And then the respect is really sort of all-encompassing.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Not just authority, but respecting yourself, respecting your teammates or your bandmates and other people around you. Okay, that's great.

utterances.text: Definitely, that's right.

utterances.text: All right. Well, um, one of the things I wanted to talk to you about sort of relates to belonging and your friends. So what kinds of things do you like to do when you get together with your friends?

utterances.text: Um, sometimes we just, you know, go to the movies, go to the beach, like I had said, or sometimes we just get together at someone's house, play some good board games and hang out.

utterances.text: Mm-hmm, and when you're hanging out with friends, is there ever alcohol involved?
