utterances.text: Yeah, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell me a little bit about how alcohol fits into sort of your social scene?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, well it's mostly just for, for parties or party settings is kind of to get things going and get everything loosened up as they say.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. And so when you go to parties, most of the time there's alcohol there?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And how often do you think you would say you're drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd say, um, on a not busy month, for instance, I'd say about like two weekends out of the month. Two or three.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So about half the time you're drinking and half the time you're not. Can you tell me what's different about the days when you choose to drink versus not to drink?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: The days that we drink are mostly, like I said, they're parties, so it's more of that whole partying and dancing and, you know, having everyone have fun. And then when we don't, it's a lot more relaxed. It's a lot more hanging out, playing board games, watching a movie it's not yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So it really depends on what the activity is, whether or not alcohol is gonna be there?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And do you notice a big difference or can you tell me about the difference in your enjoyment level at say a party versus a night you're playing board games?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I think of them as-as different, I think, you know, like in playing board games and things, it's meant to be relaxing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So it's nice to have like that kind of breather-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -versus with a party it's a lot more energetic it's, uh, after it all, it's very draining.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But in the moment it's quite fun to dance and have fun.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So there's sort of pros and cons on both sides?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What are the things that you like about drinking or like about alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, it's, you know, when we drink, we-we tend to have more fun because I guess we're not, you know, everyone's drinking together. We're a lot more loosened up and relaxed-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and not really thinking about stresses or things like that, but it can be--When it's too much drinking, it can be- can be obviously bad.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So sort of in the-the too much drinking or-or at times, can you tell me some of the less good things or not so good things about alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, a lot of times, it'll make- it'll make people stupid. [laughs] Yeah, you know, people make dumb decisions and things like that. We-we usually try to be as safe about it

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -as possible. So we'll like sleep over at a friend's house. And so that, you know, we're not driving and it's mostly within our friend group. So we're not worried about strangers putting weird things in our drinks.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But, um, definitely some of the ideas people can have when they're stup- when they're drunk and can be really stupid.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So you're trying to, like you said, not engage in really dangerous activities?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're trying to stay put, you're not driving. You're trying to stay with people that you trust. Um, but yet it sounds like there's still some-some things happening from time to time.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sometimes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Can you tell me a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I, especially don't like it whenever me or one of my friends, like we drink too much and we end up like throwing up or things like that, that I don't- that's not fun.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Throwing up is never fun.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's not.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And how often do you think that happens?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: For me, that's happened to me once. It was the first time I ever drunk and it was- it was a lot, I didn't know what I was doing. I was mixing all kinds of weird things and just kind of taking anything everyone- anyone gave me

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and that didn't end well.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But after that, I haven't- but I do have friends that still do sometimes, so I'll end up like having to take care of them or something and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It kind of puts a downer on my- on my fun.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Okay. So, on the one side, some of the fun things associated with alcohol are people are just more relaxed, sorta, um, carefree can kind of let loose a little bit more, on-on the other hand, there's a little bit more, I guess, planning involved-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -because you have to make sure that you're doing it safely or as safe as you can. And then, um, there can be some other consequences like throwing up or even if it's not you, that sometimes you're stuck your-your fun is sort of ruined when you're stuck dealing with a friend who drunk too much. Okay. And the other not so good things about the alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. People can get a little like sloppy, I guess. Like they're all loose, like with people in corners doing things that should be done in private-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and that kind of stuff.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you're kind of stuck being exposed to things you don't need to see.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Got it. Okay. Um, all right. Well, you mentioned a couple of times that you've made a few decisions to try and limit the dangerous aspect of the drinking. Why did you make those decisions?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I just- I've, you know, I have an aunt who is an alcoholic. So I-I see like the issues that are involved and I've seen movies and things I know that drunk driving is an issue-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I, you know, I wanna be as safe as possible in those terms and be in a setting where like we can let loose but still be safe like in someone's house or sort of my parents will tell me something. But-- So, I- like I know that there are dangers involved and I guess I wanna limit that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And so be where I have fun.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah, it sounds kinda similar to your, um, your value of respect to yourself.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: On the one hand, you- the drinking maybe helps with the belonging community to start.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: If there's too much, then it sort of—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Then it kind of defeats the purpose? [laughs]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right. And then with the respect, one of the things you mentioned, is really wanting to respect yourself and not sort of cross boundaries, not sort of cross lines.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, how do you think that the drinking fits in with that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: In terms of what? In terms of respect?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think, well in a way, I do think that drinking is probably a form of disrespect to my own body because I'm not putting things- I'm putting things in it that shouldn't be there.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And then-- But in terms of at- how it is I am respecting myself, I am- I'm respecting myself by like trying to stay in someone's house and like trying to limit my drinking so I don't get to that blackout like throwing up and everything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And try to, you know, let loose but still be in control of my behavior so I'm not gonna go somewhere with a person I met-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -into I don't know where to, I don't know what, and-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -things like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So you're sort of looking for that balance-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -of how much you can drink to have some of the positive benefits but not cross over.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And what have you come up with at this point? Do you have sort of a-a limit that you stick to or are you--?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I usually-- Well, I start off like I make sure that I make my own drink so I know what's in it and how much is in it. So in that way I control how much I drink. So, I usually just, you know, get one of those cups and then make one drink. And then I'll try to make it last as long as possible. And I'll be like, "All right, this is my one drink" and I'm good in that way. I still have something in my cup so people aren't gonna be like, "Oh, here. Have some more." I'd be like, "No, I'm good. I have mine," and I'll still be, you know, having some to like let loose a little.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay. And do you feel that that's working pretty well for you or do you sometimes exceed that limit or-or what do you think?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: For the most part, it works pretty well because, like I said, people, you know, people come asking me, trying to pressure me, I'll be like, "No, I'm good. I have- You know, I still have something. I'll get some later." And I never end up getting anything. Oh, but sometimes they'll be like, "Hey, let's take a shot," and everyone's gathered around like the kitchen or something ready to take a shot. And then at that point, I'll be like, "Oh, well, maybe I can take one more." And that's when I start, you know, falling into-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -way too much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, uh, uh, a portion of the time it's working well for you and another portion of the time maybe you would like-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -would like to make some adjustments-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -to-to make it a little smoother. Okay. So, kind of thinking along those lines, how important is it to you make some changes or make some adjustments to your drinking to sort of fit with your values and your goals for yourself?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I'd like to make sure that I'd, you know, in terms of respecting myself and my body, I'd like to, you know, try to drink less.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like I-I-- You know, it is nice to let loose and have fun, but I'd also like it to be so, you know, I'm not damaging my body, you know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like my liver doesn't work by the time I'm like 22.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, um, you know, have my friends on board with a similar mentality so we can kind of work at it together as a group, as a- as a community.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh. So kind of combining you alls-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -goals. Okay. So, you-you have a goal it sounds like, of actually cutting back on your drinking. How important is it to you to work on that goal and on a scale of one to ten, where one is not at all important and ten is it's the most important thing right now?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd say about like-like a six or a seven.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'd like to work on it but, you know, if I get around to it, I get around to it. If I don't, I don't.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Why do you say six or seven rather than like a four?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, because I still think it's-it's important.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I still, you know. Like I said, I don't want to hurt my body. Especially going to med school like I know how things affect your body and also affect your-your social and your school work and things like. I know that once I get to college, it's not- it's not gonna-gonna work out being, you know, drinking every weekend and then like trying to wake up early and go to school, take an exam. Like I know that's not- that's not feasible. It's not a good idea.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, looking ahead, you can't keep drinking this way and reach the goals that you have for yourself.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, how confident are you that you could cut down if you wanted to-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think I-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -on that same scale from one to ten?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think if I made the decision that I was going to, for sure, then I think definitely like a 10 I know it'd be going through.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, wow. Okay. Why do you say 10?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's just because I know that once I make the decision, I know I can do it. It's making the decision in the first place.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And so you mentioned the- you know, quite a few reasons why you would like to cut down. Um, have you thought at all about how you might go about doing that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I'm thinking of maybe like trying to convince my friends without sounding, you know, dorky or something and be like, hey, you know, let's just stay in today. Like, let's not go out or something. Or just be like, hey, I'm not like-- I'm not going to drink today. And then even if my friends do, like being okay with them, drinking around me and not doing it, and then them being okay with me drinking-- Me not drinking and them doing whatever they want.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So sort of, um, trying to plan more activities that don't involve alcohol-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and then also trying to participate in activities without drinking yourself or maybe even drinking less than you're drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Does that sound like a goal you want to work on now or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think so. I think it's-it's very feasible. I think it's possible.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, so I guess we'll talk about, um, less alcohol activities. I'm just making some notes to myself and then maybe, um, reducing the amount of drinking that you're doing if alcohol is involved. Okay. Um, so that-that goal sounds feasible, you said? Would it be okay if we met in a couple of weeks to sort of see how it's going?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think so. I think that's good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Does that sound like something you'd like to do?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I really appreciate you spending the time talking to me, you know, it sounds like you have a lot of really good goals for yourself, really ambitious goals of going to medical school and, you know, becoming a psychiatrist or, um, some-some other form of physician. Um, you're really looking forward to doing well in school so you can get there.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it sounds like you have a pretty active social life and a-a lot of friends who you feel probably would be, uh, supportive, even if you cut down on alcohol and that, you know, there's a lot of benefits you see both to your body and your health, um, your school performance, and even some of the social stuff in terms of feeling a sense of belonging without having to deal with some of the gross consequences of-of, um, drinking too much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, so yeah, you know, it really sounds to me like you have a good plan in place and as long as you're willing and-and interested in meeting again, I'd be very excited to be able to talk with you about how it's going.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I'd like to.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. Great. So I'll-I'll plan to see you then in a few more weeks.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Perfect. Nice.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great.

video_title: Motivational Interviewing: Linking Behaviors

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Would you like to answer some questions and kind of do a self-evaluation about how you're feeling around alcohol and the contraception?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So we're working on a 10 point of scale 1 to 10, 1 being not important, 10 being very important. One being not confident, one being very confident. So on a scale of 1 to 10, which number best reflects how important it is to you to drink the-- what risk limits?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I would say an eight.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You'd say an eight. Okay. And on a scale of 1 to 10, how confident are you at the present time that you can drink below risk levels?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I would say a four.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Amount of four.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And so let's look at those two. You're-you're thinking it's pretty important, but your confidence is down here, uh, a four, but it's not a one. What makes you confident that you can drink below risk levels and you remember what those are?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I think it's because you've told me I'm at risk and I have alcoholism in my family and I really don't want to go down that path. So I'm-I'm confident that I can change that at this point.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So that gives you a good reason not to drink. Okay. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, I have a group of friends that doesn't drink that I hang out with. And I think when I hang out with them, it's not an issue. So that also helps me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you have a support group that gives you the ability to have fun and still drink below risk levels?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Nope.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Now let's look at your self-evaluation of your birth control. So now we're doing the risk of pregnancy and the use of birth control. So on a scale of 1 to 10, how important is it to you to use effective birth control every time you have sex to keep from getting pregnant?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I would say an eight.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: An eight. Okay. And on a scale of 1 to 10, how confident are you at the present time that you- that you can use effective birth control?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Every time,-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Every time.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -probably a six.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Correctly as it's prescribed.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Probably a six.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Probably a six. Okay. So you're pretty confident that you can do it. And why are you a six and not a two or three?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I'm a six because I think if I drink less, I'll be more reliable with using birth control. I tend to not use it when I'm-- I drank too much and I don't really care too much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So it's kind of linked to your drinking, the fact that, um, that you can-- if you can take care of that drinking, you can take care of the-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -birth control issue and this importance comes down as your reason why you're not down here.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Very good. So it looks like, um, you're using a good method of birth control, you're just not able to use it effectively. And you've linked it back here to the drinking. So would you like to develop a plan around your alcohol use at this-- today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Before I leave?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And if you need more information, we can get that for you.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

video_title: Motivational Interviewing (MI) for Addictions Video

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So let me tell you what I normally do in this, um, this interview, and we-we'll talk for up to maybe 20 minutes or so. Normally what I do is just give some feedback from all of those questionnaires that you answered last week-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and then we just talk together about that. So, um, but I always like to just start with wherever you would like to start as well.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, yeah, I, [sigh] that, I mean, like, when I was doing those questionnaires, it was weird because, I mean, I guess I don't really think about, like, you know, the drinking being, like, this huge deal and I don't-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -ever really think about, like-like, how much I drink.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, and, like, fi- like filling out, like, how much I'm drinking every day, it was like, whoa, you know-

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -like, I just didn't ever really think about it, like, that I was-- like, if I try to actually count the drinks, it's, kind of, a lot, I mean, it's, kind of, a lot.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You were pretty shocked at what you learned about your patterns.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, yeah, 'cause, like, I also, kind of, thought that, like, I drink, like, about as much as my friends did and then, like, I went back and I was, like, talking to my roommate about it and I was, like, telling her that, you know, I was drinking, like, like 10 drinks on the weekends, like, including Thursday, so like, Thursday, Friday-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -Saturday, Sunday.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And then she was like, "Sarah, that's cra-- Like, that is crazy. Why are, you know, like, where are you drinking this?" And I was- I was like, "Well, you know, like, different places." And I-I guess, like, I don't know, my friends didn't, like, know. Anyway, it's, yeah, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, this information has opened your eyes in some ways and as you talked to your roommate about it, she was even shocked to know that you were drinking as much as you- as you realized when you did the questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and yeah, I guess it was just like, I thought that everybody was, like, doing it, you know-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -but that's not really what was going on. [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, the fact that your drinking stands out from others is clearly not something you had ever really taken into consideration before?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, so, that was the thing that, like, was really the most weird about doing those-

video_title: Motivational Interviewing: Talking With a Pregnant Woman About Her Alcohol Use

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Thank you for coming in today, Katie. I'm looking forward to getting to know you, and maybe just wanna start off with just sharing a little bit about you and what brought you in today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, sure. Um, I guess, well, my doctor referred me to see you. Um, I guess he has some concerns about, um, my- my pregnancy and- and my baby. So, um, yeah, well, I'm doing what I'm told.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you're following through on meeting with me today and you mentioned he has some concerns. Can you tell me a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, he is concerned about my alcohol intake.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm wondering if you have any concerns about that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, no.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: No. Okay. So that's- that's not been an issue for you. Uh, it is an issue for him and not for you at this point.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So what about maybe sharing a little bit about your alcohol intake and maybe a little bit about what your- what your life's like a little bit for me today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, okay. Uh, well, I guess I drink like a glass of wine at supper every night, and just to, you know, relax a little with my friends if I go out. So wine has always been a kind of a family tradition with supper. So-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So it was kind of been a part of your culture a little bit, and you know, just find alcohol, maybe takes the edge off a little bit and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and I, you know, I-I have friends who have drank during pregnancy, and-and I see articles on Facebook and-and, you know, things that show that there isn't really a clear link between, you know, abnormalities or, uh, yeah, I just- I just think it's kind of an old wives' tale. So, you know, I'm independent and I'm gonna- I'm gonna do what I want, it's my body.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't feel very comfortable with somebody telling you what you should be consuming, what kind of alcohol, and how much alcohol you should be consuming. And, um, it sounds like you've been getting some mixed messages, your doctor's saying there's no safe amount of alcohol you can drink, and asked you to come and see me. And then also, you've been checking- sounds like you've been checking things out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. You know, I've looked it up to see, you know, kinda what I can say back, you know, to support my argument.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, which is that, um, I'm going to do what I- do what I wanna do and what I know, right? So it's- yeah. I don't know, but, um, I'm here anyway. So-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you know yourself best and you wanna be sort of the boss of your body and you don't want somebody else telling you what- what's okay and what's not okay. And it seems like you're not maybe too concerned right now about your substance use.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Nope. I never have been.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm wondering if that concern is coming from, "It's been okay. I've got these messages from friends."

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: "Um, media has said it's okay to drink during alcohol. And so that concern, um, just sort of, I don't have it and, and maybe the doctor might be wrong."

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. I think so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You're not sure if he's sort of playing things up a little bit there?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, you know-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It might be a bit extreme to-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -to quit drinking. Um, I'm just wondering, have you, um, would you be open maybe to just kind of taking a look at what Canada's guidelines say about drinking? Um, is that something you'd be open to?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like right now?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What if- uh, can I show you a brochure about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I guess.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, if we take a look at the low-risk-alcohol drinking guidelines, what it says is for women, um, the safe limits are 10 drinks a week for women and 2 drinks a day. And that's if a woman isn't pregnant. And when it says in the guidelines, as far as drinking, uh, throughout pregnancy, there is no safe amount to drink during pregnancy. So really zero alcohol is, um, the woman should not be drinking any at all. And I'm just wondering what-what are your thoughts on that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know, I've-I've heard these kinds of things before, but I just- I don't see the evidence. I don't see the risk, you know, I don't, you know, if someone can like prove to me, or show a direct link or something like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So when you see it here in kind of black and white, you're not sure if this is, uh, you know, enough-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -to con- sort of convince you that-that it might be dangerous to be drinking through alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. It's just a fancy little brochure saying what I've already known, I've already heard.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you feel like, um, what the doctor's saying and this brochure just kind of feels like, yeah, it's just kind of blowing things up out of proportion a little bit.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And it sounds like you-you've got some solid information already that alcohol, you know, has been safe to-to have during pregnancy. Tell me about that information that you've-you've explored.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, I've looked up, um, different articles. Um, and I- as I said, I personally know people who haven't had any problems. Um, so that's about the extent.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. You mentioned you looked up some articles and it sounds like evidence is really important to you. So, um, those articles, is that something recent? Um, you can tell me about that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like, uh, I don't like- have like a bibliography or anything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So I can't really- I don't really know when those were published. It's just stuff I've found, supporting the way that I look at it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So you felt like, um, the information that you found supports the values that you have of being able to be independent and autonomous, to be able to make your own choice and the information that your doctor shared or spoke to you about, and then this brochure kind of feels like that's challenging sort of your values.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, it's like all this brochure is saying is that, um, the same again, the same thing that I've heard, that the limits and that there is no safe amount of drink during pregnancy, but it's like, why not?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, it's kind of like the "why" that it's like-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -I never get that information.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Wha-what's the big deal if you're drinking and—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, like what kind of issues would that cause if any?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Maybe we can kind of put that on the shelf for a moment, and we'll come back to it and sort of look at, you know, what is- what does the guidelines have to say about why. And, um, and-and I'm wondering if we can kind of just have a look for a moment at, um, your pregnancy, and is this something that you were- you were hoping to have a baby?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That was something that you'd been planning?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm wondering as far as, um, bringing the baby into the world and, you know, your future as a parent, ho-how important is it to have a healthy baby to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, it's-it's really important to me. That's a big priority of mine is to have a healthy baby and bring him or her up well and-and, you know, be a good parent.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm. What does being a good parent look like? Tell me more about that.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, not-not like being there at home with them, not being absent, um, taking care of them, feeding them, um, changing their diaper, which I'm not excited about. Um, you know, kind of the- those basics.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hmm. Kind of like protecting your baby and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -guiding your baby and-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -you know, nurturing that baby is really important to you-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -and raising your baby well?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's something that- that really matters to you and, um, I'm-I'm hearing you say that, you know, protecting your baby is important to you and at the same time, um, kind of clashes with some of the information that's in the brochure.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What do you make about that- what do you think about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, I just don't know- I just don't know where-where these brochures get their information or-or anything from, like, where's the hard evidence essentially.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You wanna see it in black and white.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You wanna know that it's the latest and the greatest kind of thing. Um, this is information that, uh, that I have been sharing with you earlier, this is the latest information evidence-based, um, on the latest research since 2011 and, um, a lot of research has gone into what is-what is okay for a mom to consume, like, alcohol. There's the-the evidence that we have, um, but in the end, you choose what's best for you and what's best for your baby. What are your- what are your thoughts on that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, it surprises me that that's based on research from out of 2011, um, and I must have missed that. I guess, you know, if it is, um, you know, I do wanna do what's best for my baby and for myself. And if I have to quit drinking, um, I guess ultimately I have to-I make that decision, um, but, um, that's a lot of, uh, information to take in today.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, kind of feels like, you know, you were making some really good decisions about your baby. You've done research and you wanna be able to bring your baby up well and take care of your baby. And I-I can see that that's really important to you. I hear you saying that and it kind of feels like this information isn't kind of what you were expecting to hear.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Nope.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What would you feel like would be helpful as far as next steps, like when you think about maybe moving away from drinking alcohol throughout the rest of your pregnancy?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, well, first things first, if I could take a brochure home maybe, um, you know, show it to my partner and-and-and get-get their support, um, I think that's really gonna help me, and kind of changing our-our habits, or, you know, putting the alcohol away, out of sight. Um, I think that's probably the best thing I can do, like, today when I get home.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, that's some really significant steps you're talking about. You're talking about putting the alcohol away, that's huge. That's-that's really big steps.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: I really want to thank you for, you know, exploring this with me today, and I'm wondering if we can kind of continue this conversation again, and talk about those steps, and how it goes with talking to your partner about giving up drinking and, um, the- giving you a chance to do some more research and, you know, maybe looking through these brochures and kind of just coming back and sharing a little bit more about, you know, what you thought about the information and what feels right for you. Is that something you'd be open to?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that- I think that would be a good idea, and maybe you could help me, yeah, with, like, ways to approach it because I think that my partner kind of has the same view that I- that I had. So-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: We definitely can cover that again on our next meeting. Thank you for coming to see me.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you.

video_title: Brief intervention: "Steve"

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Steve, before we're done with our visit today, I was wondering if you'd be willing to take a few minutes to talk about your drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay, like what?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, you filled out this survey for us today, which was great. Thank you very much. I just wanted to review a couple of things on here. I noticed that you said that you drink two to three times a week, drink three or four drinks at a time when you do drink, and weekly, um, have more drinks than that. So six or more drinks, it says on here.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Does that sound realistic?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, uh, on the weekends?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay. I just wanted to let you know, I'm a little bit concerned about your level of drinking. We know that excessive drinking can make problems worse or can actually cause health problems at times, and I was just wondering if you thought about the connection between your drinking and things like the anxiety and the insomnia that you came in with today?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, I guess I haven't really thought much of it. Um, you know, I don't really think I drink that much in the first place-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -so I have a hard time believing that it's causing my anxiety.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: In fact, on the nights when I don't drink, I-I have a harder time going to sleep.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, you're not alone, a lot of people think that drinking helps them sleep better, and in reality, drinking might make you fall asleep faster, but it has what's called this rebound effect, and this rebound effect means that you wake up, may, might wake up in the middle of the night or early in the morning and have a hard time falling back asleep.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I, yeah, I guess I do have abo-about 2:00 AM, I tend to wake up on the nights I drink too much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Well, I just wanted to just show you this little chart here. For your age as a male, you're drinking more than those at a low-risk level. Um, the low-risk level for men under 65 is no more than 14 drinks a week and no more than four a day. And, in this case, a drink is considered 12 ounces of beer, 5 ounces of wine, or an ounce and a half of distilled spirits. And you're right, you're not drinking as much as some people out there. The way you answered our questions here, you're actually falling in the high-risk category, the risky or hazardous category, category two.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Jeez, no. I didn't think I was that bad.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: That's why it's helpful to look at this and give some perspective. On a scale of 1-10, what is your readiness to change, 1 being I don't want to change at all, and 10 is I really want to change?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, this is all news to me. I've, I don't want to do anything to put myself at risk and I've always thought of myself as a pretty healthy guy. I guess I'd put myself right in the middle of the five.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, that's great. That's halfway there. What kept you from just giving it a one or two, something lower?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, you know I'm training for the marathon, and that's why I'm coming in, is because I need to be able to get my sleep back on track, but I also don't think of myself as a hazardous drinker, and I'm certainly not an alcoholic. So, that's-that's why the middle-ground, five.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay. Well, that's a good place to start. So, I heard you say your health is important, and you're getting ready to run a marathon, so you wanna be able to do what you can to make that successful. And you also were a little bit surprised that you fell into this risky or hazardous category.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, based on all that information, what are you willing to think about doing to change right now?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I-I think the natural thing would be to cut back a little on my drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So, what would that look like for you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm, um, you know, I-I guess drinking no more than maybe three or four times a week, and-and on the weekends, which is when I would drink the most, cup back to no more than five or six beers.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, okay. Well, sometimes when people aren't ready to make changes like this, it helps if they write down their goals, it gives them a chance to see them in black and white. If you were to look at this little form here and figure out where you want to go with your drinking, what would you put down as your goal?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, doing the math, I guess no more than 18 drinks a week.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So that's an improvement. So you're headed in the right direction. I do wanna let you know that with 18 drinks a week, you're still falling above this low-level risk category, and that it would be my recommendation that at some point you would fall below into this 14 or less a week. But it's an improvement, and it's a great place to start, and I really commend you for your willingness to take a look at this and try to make some improvements.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So I'm hoping that in your appointment next month, we can touch base on this and see how it's going.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.text: Um, before we get into that, I see you filled out our annual screening forms here. So if-if you're okay, can we take a minute to talk about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, great. It looks like, um, the way you filled out the alcohol form puts you into our, uh, third zone of drinking. Can you- can you tell me a little bit about your drinking habits, where you drink, what do you like to drink?

utterances.text: I drink wine-

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -mostly. Um, I go down to the little pub down the street.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: Okay. Kind of socializing?

utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hmm, for four times a week probably.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Maybe if it's on a weekend, maybe six.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Over a long-- over a period of time.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Are you serious?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Surprised, ain't you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Seven drinks in a week doesn't seem like that much?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like you're drinking a bit more than that right now.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, and I-I didn't think it was much, but that makes it look like I'm drinking way too much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. From this, uh, drinker's pyramid over on this side of the card, you can see that the-the score on your screening sheet shows that you're up in the harmful category of drinkers. utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Well, I know my drinking has increased a little since I got divorced and moved to Portland, but I-I don't think it's that much of a problem.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It doesn't feel like a problem to you right now, yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. And then the other thing I should mention, Jill, um, drinking more than these quantities, it's-it's possible it could be pushing your blood pressure up a bit, and I'm wondering if that might be affecting the difficulty we're having getting your blood pressure down right now.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I didn't realize that drinking had anything to do with blood pressure.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yeah, it can sometimes.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, well. Well, then I guess that could be a problem.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: My perspective as a doctor, it would be good if you could think about cutting back a little bit or doing something different about your drinking. What-what do you think about that?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: Okay. So on a scale of 0 to 10, 0 being not ready at all to do that and 10 being very ready, where would you lie on that scale?

utterances.text: I'd probably a 6.

utterances.text: Okay. Okay, so that sounds-- I think that's great. So why would you be up at a six and not down at a two level? What kinds of thing would push you to be there?

utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And though my son keeps telling me that I'm drinking too much, and it's scary to think that my drinking is harmful. It's a big word.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. So you've got some good reasons to try to cut back a little bit.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sounds like it to me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. And it sounds like you're willing to maybe try not going to the bar quite as much and maybe drinking a little bit less when you go to the bar.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think I can try to do that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So to what levels do you think you could do that? Where-where would you wanna go with your drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I guess I could use those numbers, and I can't make any promises, but I could try to drink less than three in a night and less than seven in a week.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That mean I can only drink two or three times a week.

utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So you'd drink maybe just a couple of times a week and maybe a little bit less on each occasion? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like I can try that, yeah.

utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't think I need to quit, but I think I can try to cut down.

utterances.text: And you think you're-you're able to cut down to those levels of no more than seven a week?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: That's what I'll shoot for.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. I think that sounds like a great step for you as your doctor. Why don't we revisit this the next time you come in to talk about your blood pressure in about six weeks or so and, um, then we can see how you're doing with it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.text: Sounds good.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Wow. And how long have you been in marching band?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Couple of years. Great. And how do you like Marching Band?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's fun. It's a- it's a lot of work, long summers taught, but it's fun.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: What are your favorite parts about it?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, I really like the-the group setting.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: You know, getting to work with my other classmates and things like that. And putting on this entire show-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -it's very exciting, very exhilarating once you're in competition.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It's very cool.

utterances.text: Cool. And do you have a lot of friends who are in band with you or-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -friends outside of band or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I have, um, you know, I have two-two separate groups. I have my friends from class and then my friends from bra-- from band.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So.

utterances.text: Great. And then, um, tell me a little bit about your family?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, well I have one brother he's older than me, about nine years older than me.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, wow.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And, uh, my parents and my dog. [laughs]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What kind of dog do you have?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: He's a golden retriever.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, nice.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Charlie.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Charlie.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: He's a big boy. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, cute. Have you had him a long time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. He's about eight years old now.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh gosh. Yeah. Okay. Very cool. And what are your plans for after high school?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, well, I'm planning on going to school. I'd like to become a doctor one day, so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Wow.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I'm interested in psychology, psychiatry, something like that, so.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You've got big dreams.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Cool. All right. Have you started thinking about schools or majors? I guess you're thinking about psychology as a major.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, psychology, I haven't really thought too about which school, I mean, I-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Everyone wants to shoot for the Ivy leagues, so [chuckles]

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right. And how about your grades?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, they're pretty good, you know, high three-point somethings.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Very good. All right. Well, what are the kinds of things do you do for fun on weekends?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Uh, I usually go out with my friends. Uh, we'll go to the movies or we'll most likely we'll just meet up at someone's house-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and just hang out and things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. When you're hanging out, is there ever alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sometimes, [chuckles] I'm gonna be honest sometimes.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh So how often do you think you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, depending on how much schoolwork there is When there's not, it might be like every other weekend or like three weekends out of the month or something like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, so you're drinking a lot?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A little, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And how much are you drinking on the days that you're-- on the days that you drink?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I don't, we don't get blackout drunk or anything. It's more of like a little tipsy kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I have gotten blackout drunk before-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -but I kind of did that, learned my lesson, didn't like it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Got it. So you've-you've had some pretty heavy drinking. What-what do you think is the most you've ever had?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like how many drinks?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, it was a good amount. It was the first time I ever drank and it was like three or four cups, but it was mixing different things.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so you don't even know.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So, I'm not-- Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, and then your friends drink too?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes. Not all of them, but some of them do.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And how much do they typically drink?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: More or less the same amount. So right now the most we'll have is maybe like one cup after that one time, but sometimes one or two, but they can be kind of heavy.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, so it's one cup, but it's not-not one drink.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Oh, it's a red, you know, typical. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It has a lot of alcohol in it.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, so gosh, you're-you're actually really drinking quite a lot. Um, you know, your level of drinking puts you in what we call a high-risk group.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, is that surprising to you?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Um, so we call it high-risk because it means that there's actually quite a bit of chances that you're gonna have some bad consequences from drinking like that. So, you know, things like, um, having car accidents, or other accidents, or getting in fights, or, you know, sexual assault, or health problems, or developing alcoholism. Have you thought about those things?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not too much, to be honest. I-I've always thought since it's, you know, within my small group of friends-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -and we usually sleep over each other's house, we don't get into the problems of drinking and driving, and possibly sexual assaults and things like that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But I haven't really thought about possible alcoholism or anything.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So it's, um, so it's good, because you're not drinking and driving, but you're still really drinking a lot. Um, and yeah. Okay. So, let's-let's talk a little bit about that, how you might be able to make some changes. Because I think you really need to- need to stop drinking like this.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So, um, do you think you could quit drinking or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I think I could. I don't need it. For instance, it-it is-- it is used as a kind of, like, let's get the party going.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: But we haven't always had it-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -obviously. So, I think it would be possible to stop drinking.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, does that mean you're gonna stop drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I would probably start off by like, because my friends are also involved, so I'd be like, "Hey, guys, I don't think I'm gonna drink today."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And kind of see how that goes. Because—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, you don't sound very much like you think that's gonna work.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. It's, you know, it's one thing to control my own drinking, and it's another thing when everyone else around me is drinking and then there's like that pressure-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -of, "Oh, they're gonna think I look stupid."

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, how are you gonna quit drinking without your friends thinking you look stupid?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, so I mean, do you think they're really good friends of yours if they're gonna give you such a hard time?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: My close ones, I know they wouldn't be, you know, have a problem with that. But the ones that I'm not that close with, but I'll still like hang out with-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -those are probably the ones that like might ostracize me for something or.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like you might be better off without them though. They’re-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: - maybe not very good friends.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Probably, might be too judgmental.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So, um, so I think we should set a goal that you're gonna stop drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And, um, I think you should probably stop as soon as possible, like this weekend.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Um, so the way this normally works is, you know, we set you a goal, and then I'll have you come back and we'll talk about it again in a couple of weeks and make sure that you actually stopped. Um, and so what do you think about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I think-- I think the possibility.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think if you make a good plan, like I think I'd be able to follow through with it.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, great. So, the plan is gonna be that you're gonna quit and, um, the friends that you have that you don't think are supportive, you're just gonna, I guess, not hang out with anymore.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. I think I can do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And then, um, you know, like, are your friends in band drinking?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, not-not really. The ones that drink more are the ones like my class friends. My band friends, we’re focused on band-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -so I can't really—

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, that might be good, is really just to focus more on band. Um, because you know, the other big concern I have for you is if you wanna go to medical school, you're not ever gonna get into medical school if you're drinking like this.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You know, like college is gonna be really hard. And especially with all those pre-med classes, you're not gonna be able to handle it drinking this much. You know, have you thought about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not too much, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. So, setting this goal then of quitting drinking is gonna be really helpful for you. And um, it sounds like i-it shouldn't be that tough really, um, especially because you can just stop hanging out with-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -the people who drink a lot, um, since you have some other friends. Um, yeah. So, do you have any questions for me or?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, what should I-- uh, yeah, I do. So what should I say like once, let's say, I hang out with my friends and they're like, "Hey, why aren't you- why aren't you drinking?"

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Like how should I go about that situation?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Well, you know, one good option would be to just review with them review with them all the bad things about alcohol. You can say, you know, "I thought about it, and I realized it's gonna mess up my schoolwork. And you know, it's really a lot of risk for my health." "I don't want to become an alcoholic." Um, you know, "I don't want to get liver disease.", "I don't want to end up driving drunk or getting into accidents-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -or getting in fights." You know, one thing you could bring up is, "I've heard a lot of stories about kids who you know, are at parties and they're drunk and acting stupid, and then people post stuff on Instagram."

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And you know, that's it for their social life. It's like over.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So—

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: And-and you know, like professional life as well.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I don't want that biting me in the butt, [chuckles] in the back.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. So I think just tell your friends you know, you realized there's always bad things about it and you don't want to do it anymore, so you're just not going to.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And then-

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: I think I can do that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: -you can tell them to stop too. You know, then that'd be really good. You'd being a good friend.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It'd be easier as-- You know, as a group we-we all work together to become better.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. Exactly. All right. Any other questions or anything else I can help with?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: No. I think- I think I'm good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. So, like I said, I'll plan to meet with you again in a couple weeks.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And make sure that you actually quit drinking.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Sound good.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Hi, Laura. So, thanks for coming in. I'm not sure how much you know about why you're here or what we're supposed to talk about. utterances.text: Uh, yeah, if it's school-related, maybe like a game or two, or go to the mall, like, to shop or go to the movies or something, and at night, maybe like a party or something if someone's throwing.

utterances.text: Okay. And what kind of hobbies do you have?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I like to read and I like to go outside and, like, take walks and, like, hike and stuff. I'm very outdoorsy, so-

utterances.text: Well, I plan to apply to college and maybe, you know, have a good career and something like that, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Oh, neat.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: -which is a little different, but-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, that's great. That's a really good goal.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah. Thanks.

utterances.text: It's, uh, hard work to get into law school. Are you doing well in school? What kind of grades do you get?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm doing okay. I'm getting mostly A's and B's, so I'm pretty good, I'm okay.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What classes are you not getting A's and B's in?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, I think all my grades are A's and B's, so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know where you're going to apply to college?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Cool. And, you know, what made you decide maybe law school or-or journalism?

utterances.text: Um, well, I'm definitely not a math or science person, so I started off by there that I started looking at careers that maybe I would like. So-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Great. Sounds like you have, like I said, really good goals and you're working hard in school. Um, you said that when you're going out with your friends, you like to hang out and shop and stuff like that and also go to parties, so do you drink alcohol?

utterances.text: Um, not really. Maybe one or two drinks at a party at the most.

utterances.text: Okay. And how often do you think you drink?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, maybe like once or twice a month at the most.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, so like once or twice a month you're having alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay, and so that's maybe like 20 times a year.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Possibly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: So that's actually kind of a lot of drinking then?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, I guess you can say that.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What do you think is the most you've ever had?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, just two drinks at a party at the most. I don't-- I don't like to drink a lot. I don't-- Getting drunk is not something that appeals to me. utterances.text: But you've been drunk before?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, no, not really, maybe tipsy, but not like drunk.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Um, so the most you've ever, ever had is two drinks in a day.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Interesting. So, do you know all the bad stuff about alcohol?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. Uh, how much do your friends drink?

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Okay. What about at these parties you're going to, are there other kids there who are drinking a lot?

utterances.speaker: client

utterances.text: And do you hang out with them?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Not really closely, like, I know who they are and I'll say hi, but not-- They're not really, like, close friends of mine.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, so, you know, even just hanging out around kids who are drinking a lot actually puts you at a lot more risk. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Um, yeah. That makes sense.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Yeah, so, there, I mean, a lot of the other dangers of drinking, like, um, not just car accidents, but you can have other accidents, you know, people, um, you know, will fall or, um, you know, break things or a lot of people actually end up breaking their bones and ending up in the emergency room because they've been drunk and falling down or, you know, as a girl, it's really important too that you're careful because you could be sexually assaulted.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: You know, especially if you've been drinking, then, you know, you're at a lot more risk because a guy can take advantage of you. Did- have you thought about that?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I have. That's, uh, one of the main reasons that I don't like to drink that much.

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: So-

utterances.speaker: therapist
utterances.text: And then, um, you know, people get in fights more often when they've been drinking too. utterances.speaker: client
